messages:
maria: escalation from Acme — embeddings endpoint intermittent 400 'dimension mismatch' + occasional 401s. They've also reported a billing spike and noticeable tail latency jumps (p50 ~1.6s -> p95 ~6s). ticket #12345, repro attached. please triage.
kevin: adding context — customer rolled model from open-embed-1024 -> open-embed-1536 last week. client SDK v0.9.1. sounds like batcher may be combining requests with different embedding sizes.
aj: quick infra peek: I see dynamic-batcher activity on shard emb-7 during the window. batcher coalesced many small reqs; there are kernel asserts about dim mismatches. also auth logs show a few token refresh failures around the same time. pulling detailed logs.
maria: repro snippet they sent — their exact curl: 
```\ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":["a","b","c"]}'\n```
They say errors only happen under sustained load (hundreds qps). Error body: `{"error":"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024"}`
kevin: that error lines up with model dim mismatch. two likely vectors: (1) client sometimes still sending requests for old model id (1024) while switching, (2) batcher is fusing requests routed to different model execs when max_batch_size/batching window lines up.
natalie: question — do we currently allow multiple model_ids into the same batch execution if kernel is compatible? If not, a routing bug could be letting mixed-model requests through. Also the 401s suggest token rotation on the client side triggering retries -> duplicate requests and billing spike.
aj: pulled logs show this sequence: `BATCHER coalesce: ids=[org/acme:open-embed-1536, org/acme:open-embed-1024] -> assigned to exec-pool emb-generic` then later `ERROR batch_exec.cpp: runtime_assert embedding_dim_mismatch expected=1536 actual=1024`. Also auth: `AUTH token_refresh_failure client_id=acme-prod, status=500` followed by client retry (no idempotency-key).
billing-bot: invoice analyzer shows ~2x embedding units for org:acme between 14:04-14:09 UTC. pattern matches retry storms. Recommend idempotency and temporary credits.
maria: for immediate mitigation: (A) ask customer to pin model id on their SDK and upgrade to SDK>=1.2.0 which auto-sets idempotency-key (B) we can route their org to a dedicated pool to avoid mixed-route batching (C) engineering to add a guard rejecting mixed-model batch coalescing at router.
kevin: I can reproduce in dev. ran a synthetic with mixed model ids: `python repro_mix.py --models open-embed-1024,open-embed-1536 --qps 250` — hit the same assert in ~25s. attaching local logs and stack: `batch_exec.cpp:line 402 runtime_assert failure`. repro suggests deterministic when small and large requests interleave.
natalie: I'll open an urgent PR to add a routing guard (reject mixed-model coalesce) and a metric `batch_mixed_model_rejections`. Also we'll add a padding-validation check before kernel dispatch to fail safe (return 503 or queue separately) instead of kernel assert. Target canary by EOD tomorrow.
aj: operationally I can move org:acme -> dedicated pool acme-ded-1 for 1 hour to remove the mixed routing pressure. Doing the move now — will monitor tail latency. :white_check_mark:
maria: onboarding note for support response to customer: 1) please ask them to upgrade SDK to >=1.2.0 and include idempotency-key in retries, 2) pin model version while we hotfix, 3) we're routing them to a dedicated pool temporarily and investigating the batcher bug, 4) billing team will review and may issue credit for confirmed duplicate charges.
billing-bot: holding potential credit until we confirm the retry duplication and the timeframe. please DM billing with ticket #12345 logs.
kevin: attaching repro script and a short log excerpt in the ticket. I also tested a quick workaround: set route option `strict_model=true` which disables cross-model coalescing and prevents the kernel assert. customer-side workaround is to pin.
maria: thanks team. next actions: natalie to open PR, kevin to paste repro logs to ticket, aj to confirm dedicated routing done and watch p95. i'll update customer with mitigation and next steps. tagging @oncall-bot to keep incident watch for 2 hours.
oncall-bot: incident watch enabled until 3302469360 UTC.
